trust_decision.summary: At the pinned commit the local HTTP control plane decides 'may this caller drive the agent?' from request headers alone: isTrustedApiRequest() admits any request whose Host is loopback or a configured trustedHosts authority and whose Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site markers are same-origin, so the Host/Origin fence IS the authorization decision. No caller identity, token or cookie is checked anywhere, and the fence's own docblock states it is not an auth layer, so any local process (and any LAN client on a trusted host) reaches session.create, settings.*, credentials.*, host.openPath and the Typert RPC lane.

landing_point.why: The advisory says 'local HTTP control-plane API'; this is the only /api route, it is where the browser-trust fence gates every control-plane call, and its own comment (lines 123-128) describes the fence plus the loopback pin as the whole defence.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP /api/* (browser RPC prefix route registered on webServer)
HTTP /api/* shared fetch handler with the PRIVILEGED_METHODS loopback pin
HTTP /<channel>/* registered through the public ctx.connection.rpc.handle API
shared /api interceptor lane registered through ctx.connection.rpc.intercept (Typert RPC /api/<service>/<method>)
public HostConnectionHandle.isTrustedRequest helper that sibling Web routes call
WebSocket upgrade GET /api/remote.mux (Typert Remote stream mux)
GET / and GET /index.html served by the SPA fallback seat
CLI dsh web startup: printed URL line and default-browser handoff

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The frontend-static package is a static-file SPA server with no RPC in it, so a solver can argue the advisory's 'control-plane API' means /api and /api/remote.mux only, and that the index page is public by definition like every other asset in the same dist.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-index static assets must stay reachable without a browser session: the shell's .js/.css and the packed .gz VFS image are fetched with no cookie, and the fixed module doc says 'Non-index assets stay public'. An over-broad fix that puts the session check on the whole frontend-static fallback breaks asset delivery and the documented empty-404/405 contract for misses.

O6_input_shapes: ?token= launch query on exactly GET / (duplicate token parameters rejected, token on any other path or non-GET rejected, constant-time comparison)
signed session cookie v1.<base64url JSON payload>.<base64url HMAC-SHA256>, bound to the request Host authority by both the cookie name (sha256 of authority) and the signed payload
header containers: Fetch Headers and node:http plain record whose values may be string, string[] or undefined
Cookie header carrying unrelated cookies beside the generated one, plus malformed segments and extra '=' bytes
cookie time variants: expired, issued in the future, expiresAt <= issuedAt, and a lifetime longer than cookieMaxAgeDays
HEAD vs GET for the 303/401 responses, and missing or unparsable Host authority

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second WebSocket upgrade route (for example /api/events.mux carrying forwarded Remote events only) that copies the old isTrustedRequest(req, 'trusted-host') gate, or no gate at all
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: upgrade handlers are a separate route table from the /api prefix route, so a new lane under /api inherits nothing; the file already shows the pattern to copy

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another static/SPA seat (a second bundle or plugin UI shipping its own dist) that renders index without calling authorizeIndex
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fallback seat is a generic webserver feature claimed by one owner, and serveStatic is an exported function whose old signature has no authorization parameter

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second launcher/profile (an editor integration or ACP-to-web bridge) that prints or opens localWebUrl(ctx) instead of connection.authenticatedUrl(...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the URL line is bundle glue rather than a route, and copying the launch sequence without the token leaves a server nobody can authenticate to

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a direct in-process lane composed with createSharedFetchHandler that skips the route handler that now authenticates
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: that file already documents a deliberately fence-free direct lane, so a new transport would copy it

O9_family: CWE-807 reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision: request headers (Host/Origin) stand in for authentication, giving an authentication bypass of the local HTTP control plane

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm workspace (pnpm-lock.yaml); tsdown for library builds, tsx for source launch, vitest for specs; per-package tsconfig.host.json / tsconfig.client.json

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the existing Host/Origin trust fence to the remaining routes (or add every method to the PRIVILEGED_METHODS loopback pin) instead of introducing a caller credential.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/experimental/webworker-runtime/src/worker-host.ts:366-377 composes the same /api fetch handler for an in-process postMessage tunnel with the fence deliberately left out; it is not an HTTP route, so it is outside this advisory's local-HTTP scope and was not pursued.

packages/client/hmr/src/index.ts:186 (dev /plugins/events SSE) and packages/webhook/webhook-github/src/index.ts:59 (signed GitHub webhook route) are unrelated web routes on the same server; noted only, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb: the checkout size cannot be measured without running commands (no shell in this session); the source tree is clearly far above 5 MB but the exact figure and the 1.5 GB giant threshold were not measured, so no tiny_repo/giant_repo flag was raised.

O7: at the pinned commit the guard consults request headers only; the durable signing secret lives in the credential store packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:1-35 and the fixed check reads it per request, but browser-auth.ts is a new file and cannot be cited at the pinned commit.
